Estimate isochrones from a given location

Source: R/isochrone.R
isochrone.Rd

The areas (polygon_output = TRUE) or the street segments (polygon_output = FALSE) reached from each origin within each cutoff, by one street mode ("WALK", "BICYCLE" or "CAR") or by public transport (see travel_time_matrix() for the modes). Package 'sf' is required.

Usage

isochrone(
  network,
  origins,
  mode = "transit",
  mode_egress = "walk",
  cutoffs = c(0, 15, 30),
  zoom = 10,
  departure_datetime = NULL,
  polygon_output = TRUE,
  time_window = 10L,
  max_walk_time = Inf,
  max_bike_time = Inf,
  max_car_time = Inf,
  max_trip_duration = 120L,
  walk_speed = 3.6,
  bike_speed = 12,
  max_rides = 3,
  max_lts = 2,
  draws_per_minute = 5L,
  seed = NULL,
  percentiles = NULL,
  n_threads = Inf,
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network().

origins

A data.frame with columns id, lon and lat (WGS 84), or a POINT sf with an id column, in any coordinate reference system (reprojected to WGS 84, see travel_time_matrix()).

mode

A character vector, the transport modes (default "transit"): one of "WALK", "BICYCLE" or "CAR", and for public transport "TRANSIT" or some of its modes (see travel_time_matrix()).

mode_egress

A string, the mode from the last stop to the destination: "WALK" (the default), "BICYCLE" or "CAR". Ignored without public transport.

cutoffs

A numeric vector, the travel times in minutes that delimit the isochrones. Values are sorted and duplicates removed; 0 is added and at least one value must be greater than 0. Defaults to c(0, 15, 30).

zoom

A number from 9 to 12: the Web Mercator zoom level of the travel-time grid polygons are interpolated from (only used with polygon_output = TRUE). Defaults to 10 (cells of about 153 metres at the Equator).

departure_datetime

A POSIXct, the departure date and time (see the section "Date and time"). Required with public transport.

polygon_output

A logical. TRUE (the default) for polygon isochrones, FALSE for the street segments reached.

time_window

An integer, the number of departure minutes, from departure_datetime on, over which travel times are computed. Defaults to 10.

max_walk_time, max_bike_time, max_car_time

The maximum time in minutes on foot, by bicycle and by car. Each limit applies to each leg on its own (15 minutes to reach the first stop and another 15 from the last), and to the whole trip when that mode is the only one. Inf, the default, leaves only max_trip_duration.

max_trip_duration

Not used: the trip limit comes from max(cutoffs).

walk_speed, bike_speed

Average speeds in km/h, 3.6 and 12 by default.

max_rides

An integer, the maximum number of public transport rides in a trip. Defaults to 3.

max_lts

An integer from 1 to 4, the highest level of traffic stress a cyclist rides on (see the section "Level of traffic stress"). Defaults to 2.

draws_per_minute

An integer, the Monte Carlo draws per departure minute (see the section "Departures and Monte Carlo draws"). Defaults to 5.

seed

An integer seed for the Monte Carlo draws, or NULL (the default: the draws differ from call to call). With a seed, the same inputs give the same results whatever n_threads.

percentiles

An integer vector of up to 5 values from 1 to 99, the travel time percentiles to make polygons for (one set per percentile). NULL (the default) means 50. Must be NULL with polygon_output = FALSE.

n_threads

The number of threads; Inf (the default) uses all cores (two under R CMD check when it limits the cores).

verbose, progress

Logicals, checked but without effect: no progress counter or routing log is printed.

Value

An sf table in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). With polygon_output = TRUE, one POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON per origin, percentile and cutoff, with columns id, isochrone (the cutoff), percentile (such as "p50") and polygons; rows by origin, percentile and cutoff (descending). Each polygon covers the whole area reached from 0 up to its cutoff. With polygon_output = FALSE, one LINESTRING per street segment reached, with columns id, edge_index, osm_id, isochrone (the smallest cutoff at or above the segment's travel time), travel_time_p50, the segment's attributes from street_network_to_sf() (from_vertex, to_vertex, street_class, length, walk, car, car_speed, bicycle, bicycle_lts) and geometry; rows by origin, then by band and travel time, both descending.

Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package). An sf result keeps its geometry column and EPSG:4326 and takes the same data frame class: an sf tibble, a plain sf data frame, or, with "data.table", an sf data.table where the section "Class of the results" of peabiru-package says so. With "data.table", the polygons are an sf data.table and the lines a plain sf data frame.

Details

Polygon isochrones are traced from the travel times from each origin to the centres of a regular grid of Web Mercator pixels covering the network (see zoom): the bands from 0 to each cutoff are traced over that grid by marching squares (the algorithm of isoband::isobands()), grouped into polygons with holes (as isoband::iso_to_sfg() groups them) and passed to sf::st_make_valid() (see the section "Repair of the polygons" for the case in which spherical geometry changes their area). The order of the rings and the vertex each one starts at are those 'isoband' gives on each platform, which follow the C++ library it is built with (libc++ on macOS, libstdc++ on Linux and Windows); between platforms the polygons differ in that order and, by the system's sinh() and atan(), in the last bits of some latitudes.

Line isochrones are the travel times from each origin to the centroid of every street segment (sf::st_centroid() of the edges of street_network_to_sf()), each segment in the band of the smallest cutoff at or above its travel time.

max_trip_duration is not used: the trip limit is the largest cutoff (plus 10 minutes for polygons, so that the outer band is interpolated like the inner ones).

Repair of the polygons

The traced polygons go through sf::st_make_valid(). With spherical geometry on (sf::sf_use_s2(), sf's default), that repair snaps the vertices and, in a polygon of many parts and holes, can return an area that is not the traced one: of 438 isochrones of Porto Alegre and Helsinki, 17 came out between 0.1% and 9.5% larger or smaller. When the spherical repair changes the area of a polygon by more than one part in 10,000, the polygons of that origin are repaired on the plane instead (which leaves the area as traced) and a warning of class peabiru_isochrone_repair names them. options(peabiru.isochrone_repair = "spherical") keeps the spherical repair in every case, without the warning.

See also

Other routing functions: accessibility(), arrival_travel_time_matrix(), detailed_itineraries(), expanded_travel_time_matrix(), travel_time_matrix()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))
departure <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")

# polygons: the areas reached on foot within 10 and 20 minutes
iso <- isochrone(network, points[1, ], mode = "WALK",
                 cutoffs = c(0, 10, 20), departure_datetime = departure,
                 n_threads = 2)
iso
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 3 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -46.63902 ymin: -23.56588 xmax: -46.6198 ymax: -23.54762
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   id              isochrone percentile                                  polygons
#>   <chr>               <dbl> <chr>                                  <POLYGON [°]>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff        20 p50        ((-46.62941 -23.56462, -46.62804 -23.564…
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff        10 p50        ((-46.62804 -23.55958, -46.62666 -23.559…

# lines: the street segments reached by public transport
iso_lines <- isochrone(network, points[1, ], mode = "TRANSIT",
                       cutoffs = c(0, 10, 20), polygon_output = FALSE,
                       departure_datetime = departure, seed = 42,
                       n_threads = 2)
head(iso_lines)
